newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SIERRA LEONE ASKED TO ENSURE SAFETY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SIERRA LEONE ASKED TO ENSURE SAFETY.

text.p: Sierra Leone have been asked to ensure that their home soccer stadium is a safe place to play.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) said on Sunday they want a guarantee of good security and organisation in Freetown for Sierra Leone's future home matches in the African Nations Cup qualifiers.
Sierre Leone have until July 10 to comply. Otherwise their remaining two home matches could be switched to neutral Mali.
Their team had their group four home match against Tunisia postponed last weekend because of fighting following the recent coup d'etat in the west African country.
CAF have ordered it to be played on Wednesday, July 23 in Freetown, four days before Sierra Leone are scheduled to host Guinea in the final qualifiying match in the group.
"In case of a negative response or no reaction from the Sierra Leone Football Association, the two matches will be played in Bamako, Mali," a CAF communique said.
Sierra Leone need to win both matches to stand any chance of qualifying for the Cup finals in Burkina Faso next year.
They have lost both away games in the three-nation group. Guinea lead with six points, followed by Tunisia with three.
The top two finishers in the group qualify for the Nations Cup in February.
